recent_posts.title: We needed a screenshot pipeline; we got a design QA tool instead
recent_posts.summary: Maintaining up-to-date product screenshots for docs and marketing is a constant burden. Calibre solved this by building an automated screenshot pipeline using Playwright that generates 585+ screenshots across all themes (light/dark), viewports (desktop/mobile), and account states in just a few minutes. Each scenario is a thin Playwright test case, and parallel execution with 10 headless browser tabs keeps the whole run fast. An unexpected benefit emerged: viewing all screenshots together in a file browser created a 'lightboard' effect that revealed UI inconsistencies invisible during normal navigation — inconsistent margins, spacing, and alignment — turning the pipeline into an accidental design QA tool that helped ship a polished dark mode and a new RUM product.

recent_posts.title: UX Rating measures what share of your users have a good experience
recent_posts.summary: Calibre's UX Rating metric answers a simple but critical question: what percentage of real users are having a good experience on your site? Unlike Lighthouse scores or APM dashboards, UX Rating evaluates full user sessions using Core Web Vitals and TTFB, bucketing experiences into Good, Needs Improvement, or Poor. The post explains how the Good% metric drives action across teams — from developers catching regressions to executives correlating it with NPS and conversion. A real-world example shows how a missing cache header dropped Calibre's own Good sessions from 85% to 34%, and how UX Rating helped pinpoint and fix the issue quickly.

recent_posts.title: Real User Monitoring: Focus, depth, and clarity from real browser sessions
recent_posts.summary: Calibre has launched Real User Monitoring (RUM) on all plans, including the free trial. Unlike competitors' sprawling APM products, Calibre RUM is designed to be focused, privacy-first, and lightweight. It captures Core Web Vitals and UX signals from anonymized browser sessions, ranks pages by traffic and impact, provides element-level attribution (identifying specific DOM elements causing poor LCP, INP, or CLS), and segments audience data by country, device, browser, and OS. RUM complements Calibre's existing synthetic and CrUX monitoring, giving teams three data sources for web performance. Setup requires a single script tag, with predictable session-based pricing starting at 5,000 sessions per month.

recent_posts.title: Track real user Core Web Vitals data with CrUX Dashboard
recent_posts.summary: The CrUX Dashboard allows teams to track real user data without additional costs or complexity. It relies on Chrome User Experience Report (CrUX) data and provides quick success/failure status updates for Core Web Vitals metrics. The dashboard also helps identify trends and target web performance improvements.

recent_posts.title: Psychology of Speed: A Guide to Perceived Performance
recent_posts.summary: Perceived performance refers to how fast or responsive a website or app feels compared to how fast or responsive it is. Factors affecting perceived performance include emotional state, age, complexity of task, input mode, and interface feedback. Optimizing actions people perform most frequently and providing appropriate feedback can improve perceived speed. Attention spans are categorized based on response time, and appropriate loading indicators can be chosen based on wait time. Strategies for preventing sudden page movements and unresponsive pages are also discussed. Design rooted in behavioral psychology can contribute to better performance and user experience.

recent_posts.title: Easily investigate page performance with Snapshot Overview
recent_posts.summary: Calibre's Snapshot Overview provides clarity of performance data and helps identify the sources of slowness in web pages. It separates Web Vitals metrics, grades measurements according to Google's recommendations, provides test progression history, and showcases key metrics related to the page rendering process. It also allows customization of the request table for detailed inspection of requests.

recent_posts.title: What is a CDN? An Unbiased Guide to Content Delivery Networks
recent_posts.summary: A content delivery network (CDN) is one of the best ways to improve the performance and reliability of your site. It can help you boost page speed, fend off denial of service attacks, and optimise your content for faster delivery. There is a lot to choose from if you’re in the market for a CDN.

recent_posts.title: Time to First Byte: What it is and How to Make Improvements
recent_posts.summary: Time to First Byte is a metric that reflects how quickly a browser can connect and download data from your servers. Poor TTFB indicates that your servers aren’t responding quickly enough, which can cause cascading performance issues for the entire page-loading process.
